A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DISRetrieval despite the changed title and format. All 21 pages of v1 and 20 pages of v2, including appendices, equations, tables and rendered figures, support reliable matching and comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original QASPER and QuALITY retrieval and question-answering results, component ablations and appendix analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains original experimental results and adds NarrativeQA evaluation, full-document evidence comparisons, timing measurements and threshold sensitivity results.

M1.justification: Equation 2 and Algorithm 2 replace v1's below-threshold text concatenation in paragraph trees with fmerge(v), which collapses short subtrees into single leaves. Algorithm 2 retains concatenation at the document level. The parser, encoders, tree integration and ranked Top-K retrieval otherwise remain, making this a targeted procedural revision.

E1.justification: V2 adds evaluation on NarrativeQA books and movie scripts: 10,577 questions over 355 test documents, averaging 51,372 words and reaching 346,902 words (Table 6). This substantially extends task and length coverage beyond the retained QASPER and QuALITY evaluations. RST-DT parser training remains.

E2.justification: Flatten-chunk, flatten-sentence, RAPTOR and Bisection remain the retrieval comparators, including on NarrativeQA. V2 Table 2 additionally introduces full-document-only generation and gold-evidence-only generation as reference comparisons for evidence-augmented question answering.

E3.justification: The reported QuALITY threshold changes from 100 to 50; this establishes a setting revision without establishing that experiments were rerun. New protocols include NarrativeQA BLEU-1/ROUGE-L/METEOR evaluation, Llama3.1-8B-Instruct generation with full-document and evidence controls, timing across 10,000–100,000-word documents, and a threshold sweep under fixed SBERT/UnifiedQA-3B/400-word conditions. Existing QASPER and QuALITY splits remain.

E4.justification: V2 adds analyses of whether retrieved evidence helps with full-document access (Section 4.3, RQ2), preprocessing scalability (Appendix C.1), and threshold sensitivity across three datasets (C.4). It removes v1's answer-type breakdown and associated failure analysis (E.3, Table 6). Retrieval-strategy, summarizer, parser-training, Top-K and multi-granularity analyses are retained, with some results revised.

E5.justification: V2 Appendix C.1 newly states that timing measurements use ten sampled documents per length range and report averages with standard deviations. V1 has no corresponding uncertainty reporting. This concerns variation across documents; neither version supplies repeated-seed uncertainty or significance tests for the main QA results.

E6.justification: Many DISRetrieval scores change while the main baseline scores remain identical. For QASPER with SBERT and 200-word retrieval, F1/Recall changes from 28.45/61.28 to 28.66/61.76 (Table 2). V2 adds NarrativeQA results of 25.59 BLEU, 30.26 ROUGE and 21.21 METEOR, full-document evidence results, and timing/threshold outcomes; it removes answer-type scores. Revised QuALITY scores accompany changed merging and threshold settings, so they are not same-protocol gains.

T1.justification: Equation 2 and the corresponding appendix definition change the below-threshold operation from assigning concatenated text to transforming a subtree through fmerge. The parser equations and training loss are retained. Newly displayed integration, encoding and cosine-scoring equations formalize existing operations; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: V1 claims the first use of discourse information for retrieval-based long-document understanding; v2 narrows this to the first systematic RST approach for long-document question answering. V2 also drops the contribution's specific 'up to 4%' retrieval-gain claim. The three central innovations and claimed benefit of discourse structure remain.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive arguments that precise evidence remains valuable with full-document access, preprocessing costs can be amortized across queries, and appropriate subtree merging depends on sentence completeness and narrative fragmentation. It removes v1's explanation of zero unanswerable-answer scores for GPT-4.1-mini and Deepseek-v3. The existing parser-quality, simple-threshold and evaluation-metric limitations largely survive relocation.

D1.justification: V2 discloses the timing study's single-A800-80G and vLLM setup and expands dataset specifications. Most existing model, hardware and prompt details remain. However, v1's statement that code and datasets are publicly available, with a project repository link, becomes a future code/model-release promise without that link. The PDFs establish this disclosure change, not actual external availability.

R1.justification: V2 adds QA-background references including SQuAD, CoQA, SCROLLS and LongBench, and RST foundations/parsing references including Mann and Thompson, Marcu, Kobayashi et al. and Maekawa et al. References such as Hearst and Eisenstein disappear. These changes broaden the background while retaining the central positioning against flat retrieval and semantic hierarchical methods such as RAPTOR.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, method exposition and conclusion undergo extensive rewriting around long-document QA. Method subsections are reorganized, limitations move out of the appendix, appendices are reordered, and an Ethical Statement and expanded enhancement explanation appear. This substantially changes the narrative and document organization beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: V2 changes the document from a single-column Letter layout to a two-column A4 layout, extensively resizing and relocating displays. V1 Figure 3 becomes appendix Figure 5; Table 2 gains a generation panel; NarrativeQA, timing and threshold displays are added; and the answer-type table disappears. Ablation panels and histogram axes are also redrawn.

improvement.justification: NarrativeQA, the full-document controls, and the runtime and threshold analyses strengthen evidence for long-document applicability, retrieval value and parameter choices. The net gain is limited by removal of answer-type failure results and weaker code-access disclosure. V2 also introduces documentation inconsistencies: Appendix A.3/Figure 5 still describes concatenation despite the merging revision, and Section 4.2 quotes 40.24 where Table 1 now reports 40.51. Overall, the added empirical checks provide a modest quality improvement despite these losses.
